title: Validity Schedule — Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
Every instrument of **Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers** is valid for a fixed number of calendar months counted from its expiry anchor. The expiry anchor is either the issue date of the original ticket the value came from or the issue date of the credit itself. Some instruments also require that travel on a ticket paid with the credit begin by the expiry date, and every instrument states whether value returned from a refunded or cancelled ticket paid with it comes back with the original expiry date.

## Schedule of validity figures

| Instrument | Validity (calendar months) | Validity counted from | Travel must also begin by the expiry date | Returned value keeps the original expiry date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Residual Travel Credit | 12 | original ticket issue date | No | Yes |
| Crestline Flight Credit | 12 | original ticket issue date | No | Yes |
| Crestline Trip Credit | 12 | credit issue date | No | Yes |
| Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate | 12 | credit issue date | Yes | Yes |
| Crestline Disruption Voucher | 12 | credit issue date | Yes | Yes |
| Crestline Denied Boarding Voucher | 12 | credit issue date | No | Yes |

## Notes to the schedule

1. **Validity.** The figure is the number of calendar months of validity counted from the expiry anchor, as a whole number of months.
2. **Validity counted from.** "Original ticket issue date" means the issue date of the source ticket shown on the credit; "credit issue date" means the date the credit itself was issued.
3. **Travel must also begin by the expiry date.** Where the column reads Yes, travel on a ticket paid with the credit must also begin by the expiry date, not only the booking. Where it reads No, only the booking is tied to the expiry date.
4. **Returned value keeps the original expiry date.** Where the column reads Yes, value returned from a refunded or cancelled ticket paid with this credit is re-issued with the original expiry date.

## Reading the schedule by column

- Two instruments count validity from the original ticket issue date: the Crestline Residual Travel Credit and the Crestline Flight Credit. The other four count it from the credit issue date.
- Two instruments tie the start of travel to the expiry date: the Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate and the Crestline Disruption Voucher.
- All six instruments carry 12 months of validity and all six return re-issued value with the original expiry date.

## Illustration (hypothetical dates)

A Crestline Flight Credit issued in May from a ticket first issued on 10 March of the same year counts its 12 months from 10 March, the original ticket issue date. A Crestline Trip Credit issued on 10 May counts its 12 months from 10 May, its own issue date. The dates are examples only.
